errors.text: The proposed example, CoCrFeMnNi, is a quinary Cantor alloy rather than the target quaternary equiatomic FeNiCrMn alloy.
The hypothesis replaces the target single-crystal molecular-dynamics regime of 10^8–10^10 s^-1 and 10–600 K with micrometer-grained specimens tested at 10^-4–10^-1 s^-1 and up to 1000 K.

It locates strain-rate-insensitive yielding above 800 K and attributes it to diffusion-assisted climb or grain-boundary sliding, whereas the target result is rate-insensitive yield within 10^8–10^10 s^-1 at the simulated temperatures and is governed by dislocation nucleation.

It proposes competing nanotwinning and bulk FCC-to-HCP transformation, while the target mechanism is Shockley-partial slip producing local stacking-fault-associated HCP signatures without twinning or bulk transformation.
The cited evidence is predominantly from quinary bulk creep or nanowire systems and therefore does not directly support the claimed behavior of the target quaternary bulk single crystal.
